assertions.evidence: subscription.py computes an anniversary date in code and skips the model when not past it: "anniversary = date(...); if as_of <= anniversary: return SubscriptionAssessment(False, None)".

Only the cancellation reason is sent to the model: assess_subscription calls "model(reason)" and the test asserts model.assert_called_once_with("Taking a break"); openrouter payload sets messages[1]["content"] to the reason.

The model question is to classify likely return ('likely'/'unlikely'/'unclear') and is only invoked after the code threshold: system prompt says "Classify whether a customer's cancellation reason suggests they will return" and test_anniversary_boundary_skips_model shows the model isn’t called until past one year.
